Check the API

How to Use the LM Studio Local API

Start LM Studio’s server from the Developer tab. For an OpenAI-compatible client, set the base URL to http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 if the server is using port 1234. Get the exact model ID from /v1/models, then send a small request to /v1/chat/completions before connecting your app.

  1. Start the server on localhost
  2. Check the base URL and list models
  3. Send the first chat request
  4. Troubleshoot a failed client
  5. Check the locally verified example

Start the LM Studio server on localhost

Download a chat model in LM Studio. Open Developer, start the server and note its port. Keep the server bound to your machine for this test. If you use the CLI instead, the following command explicitly selects localhost and port 1234.

lms server start --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 1234
lms server status

Replace the port in later commands if yours differs. With the separate headless installer, start the LM Studio daemon before starting the HTTP server.

Where does the first request fail?

Check responseCheck model IDsRun one chat

Find the OpenAI-compatible base URL and model ID

Set an app’s base URL to the address ending in /v1 if the app adds endpoint paths itself. In a direct HTTP call, use the complete route.

curl --noproxy '*' -fsS http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/models

Use an exact data[].id for a chat model. LM Studio’s model list documentation notes that downloaded models can appear when Just-In-Time loading is enabled. To see what is actually loaded in memory, use lms ps. If needed, load a downloaded model from the Developer tab or with lms load.

LM Studio’s own REST API has a separate prefix, /api/v1. Use that only when the client expects LM Studio’s native routes. An OpenAI-compatible client usually expects /v1.

Send an OpenAI-compatible chat request

Replace YOUR_MODEL_ID with the exact compatible ID. Use a short prompt and wait for a complete response before trying streaming.

curl --noproxy '*' -fsS --max-time 60 \
  http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model":"YOUR_MODEL_ID",
    "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly LOCAL_OK and nothing else."}],
    "temperature":0,
    "max_tokens":32,
    "stream":false
  }'

Check choices[0].message.content, the returned model and the finish reason. If you use the streaming mode, check that the client handles the final event as well as incremental text.

If the local server requires authentication, add the Bearer token issued by LM Studio. Use the local server’s token. See LM Studio API authentication.

Why your LM Studio client cannot connect

  • Connection refused. Check that the server is running and that the app uses its exact port. A client in a container or on another machine has a different localhost.
  • 404 or an unexpected response. Check whether the app added a second /v1, used /api/v1, or expects another API. Compare its request path with the direct commands above.
  • Authentication error. Check whether the server requires an API token, then confirm the client sends it in an Authorization header.
  • Models list works, but chat fails. Match the model ID and ensure it supports chat. Check load or memory errors in LM Studio. The models list alone cannot confirm successful inference.

What a verified local request looked like

On November 27, we loaded a small Qwen model under the ID ipunk-small and ran LM Studio on loopback port 1235. The compatible model list contained that ID. The non-stream request returned it as the response model and returned LOCAL_OK. The streamed request also returned LOCAL_OK and ended with [DONE].

Download the recorded loopback result or download the Python probe and run it from the download directory. Use the model ID and port from your own server. If you enabled authentication, provide your token via the LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY environment variable.

python3 probe-local-api.py --label lmstudio \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:1235/v1 \
  --model ipunk-small --output lm-studio-check.json

The recorded test used a preloaded model with network access restricted to loopback.
